fields.System.Title: OUT-2 — Allocation
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Decide which specific stock fulfils which order line, and reserve it — correctly, under
concurrency, with the right batch.

Scope

In. Allocation strategy, partial allocation and backorder, FEFO, locking, re-allocation
after adjustment, deallocation, shelf life rules, location preference.

Out. Creating the reservation rows themselves — that is
[INV-5](../INV/INV-5-reservations.md). Allocation decides; inventory records.

Design notes

This is the feature with the most subtle bugs in the system. Treat every story here as
carrying a mandatory concurrency test.

The locking sequence that works:

`
find candidate stock (unlocked read, for shortlisting only)
sort the chosen location IDs <- prevents deadlock
LOCK those balance rows
RE-CHECK availability under the lock <- this is the step people skip
create reservations
COMMIT
`

Skipping the re-check makes every test pass and production fail on the first busy morning.

Never allocate from a projection. Reading product_availability to decide whether to
promise stock is how you sell the same unit twice. Projections are for looking.

Keep the locked section short. No external calls, no slow queries. A long-held lock on a
popular product is a warehouse-wide queue.

OUT-205 closes a gap people forget. A downward adjustment can leave an order allocated
against stock that no longer exists. Without a subscription to inventory.stock_adjusted, the
picker discovers it at the shelf.

Start dumb. Stage 2 allocation is "oldest receipt date first". Shelf life rules, location
preference, and customer rules arrive at Stage 3 once real order patterns exist.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Double allocation of the last unit | [doc 09 §4.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Deadlock from inconsistent lock ordering | [doc 09 §4.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Allocating from a stale projection | [doc 09 §12](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| FEFO ignored for a mixed-batch location | [doc 09 §4.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Stock adjusted after allocation | [doc 09 §4.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Partial allocation leaving an ambiguous state | [doc 05 WF 4](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Long-running allocation holding locks | [doc 09 §4.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
